📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • has declared an internal “Code Red” to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures following the nearly 24-hour outage that took down Exchange Online and other Microsoft 365 services earlier this month, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters today.
  • According to recent reports, the outage on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described the outage as the most customer-affecting incident in the history of Exchange Online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:44 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Microsoft Corp. has declared an internal “Code Red” to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures following the nearly 24-hour outage that took down Exchange Online and other Microsoft 365 services earlier this month, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters today.

According to recent reports, the outage on Nov. 12 and 13 also disrupted Outlook, Teams and the Copilot artificial intelligence assistant, affecting governments from Australia and Japan to the U.S., delaying trading firms and disrupting airline communications. The designation signals the most severe and urgent level of alert inside Microsoft, according to the report.

It has been revealed that in a memo to staff on Friday, Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, described the outage as the most customer-affecting incident in the history of Exchange Online. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team,” Henderson wrote. He also conceded that the work done over the years had not been enough to protect the manufacturer on the day of the outage.

Sources indicate that engineers working the incident faced a “fog of war,” according to a separate memo sent on Monday by Amanda Silver, corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ. Silver’s memo describes responders exchanging more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats, with diagnostic data spread across fragmented internal tracking systems.

The Code Red covers five workstreams set out by Silver, including load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft has also set a target of resolving future incidents worldwide within an hour, with AI agents to be used to help engineers diagnose system health data more quickly.

How long it takes to push out fixes is another issue raised by Henderson. Writing in an earlier memo this month, Henderson said one urgent production fix had taken five to six days to reach worldwide saturation, while for urgent security challenges the goal is to go from detection to safe worldwide deployment within an hour, something he admitted the firm has yet to achieve. Henderson also plans to hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team that oversees the engineering group responsible for the underlying Microsoft 365 services, along with weekly reviews of the corrective work.

The outage itself was blamed by Microsoft on a defect introduced in July in a fix that had been prepared for its Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal Windows process was found to exhaust processor and memory resources on the servers, leaving more than 80% of them unresponsive at the worst point, according to Microsoft’s preliminary post-incident report. Microsoft, whose Chief Executive Satya Nadella has publicly apologized for the disruption, has mentioned the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents.

Silver’s memo also cites Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, who told a Code Red review that the affected component had seen “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures.”.

Speed comes with its own risks, according to security experts. “What concerns me is that speed and safety pull against each other,” Waseem Ahmed, head of engineering at AI security operations startup Secure.com, told SiliconANGLE. In his view, a pipeline able to push a fix to the world in an hour “can push a mistake in an hour.”.

Geographic traffic partitioning, which Ahmed stated limits how far a single bad change can travel, is the one of the five Code Red workstreams he would be watching.

Darin Fredde, senior director and offensive security evangelist at autonomous penetration testing company Ridge Security Technology Inc., noted that “an organization may have a recovery plan but still struggle to execute it if the tools needed to recover depend on the service that has failed.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.
  • Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion.
  • Industry observers note that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 17, 2026 at 11:00 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 7:47 am.

Sila, a startup producing next-generation battery materials, announced a long-term customer agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America potentially worth more than $1 billion. To meet demand from Panasonic and other buyers, the firm prepares to expand its plant in Moses Lake, Wash., supporting roughly 500 additional manufacturing and construction jobs over the coming years.

Industry observers note that panasonic, a battery supplier to Tesla, will buy Sila’s Titan Silicon anode material for its U.S.-made battery cells. The silicon-carbon composite can replace some or all of the graphite in lithium-ion battery anodes to improve performance.

It has been revealed that sila began operations at its Moses Lake plant last year and has about 100 full-time employees at the site. The facility is still scaling up production, with initial capacity designed to supply batteries totaling about 2 gigawatt-hours — enough for roughly 20,000 to 50,000 EVs, depending on how the material is used.

The expansion will increase that capacity to tens of gigawatt-hours, said Gene Berdichevsky, Sila’s co-founder and CEO.

“This is a really crucial blueprint for reindustrializing the U.S.,” he stated. “We have to take latest technology and leapfrog China, not just copy what they’ve done over the last 20 years.”.

While the U.S. has expanded battery manufacturing, it still depends heavily on overseas suppliers for core materials and technologies, Berdichevsky said. Sila aims to strengthen that domestic supply chain with higher-performing components.

It has been revealed that batteries support industries central to energy independence and national security. They power EVs, consumer devices, drones, robotics and hardware deployed in space, and provide backup electricity for data centers.

According to recent reports, berdichevsky said Titan Silicon can help a battery store 20%–40% more energy in the same space, cut recharging time roughly in half and deliver more power than a battery using a conventional graphite anode. The anode itself is also much lighter and smaller.

It has been revealed that in August, Sila received a conditional federal loan commitment of up to $1.4 billion through the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital to expand domestic battery technology manufacturing. The company must meet financial, legal, technical and other requirements before the loan can be finalized.

Recent findings suggest that the startup previously received a $100 million grant during the Biden administration under a similar initiative to increase U.S. energy independence. Those funds helped build its plant in Washington.

It has been revealed that the tech giant has also raised $1.6 billion from private investors, including a $300 million round confirmed in July. The 15-year-old company is valued at $2.27 billion, according to PitchBook.

Seattle-area startup Group14 also makes a silicon-carbon anode material. It operates a smaller-scale manufacturing facility at its Woodinville, Wash., headquarters and produces commercial-scale volumes at a plant in South Korea.

According to recent reports, group14 has partially completed its Moses Lake manufacturing site but repeatedly delayed the start of production. It now targets mid-2027 to bring the first of two production units online, with no firm completion date for the second. It recently confirmed plans for a factory in Spain.

Growth is key to bringing down costs and making Sila’s technology competitive in mass-market batteries, Berdichevsky stated.

“This is really the beginning of chapter three for our company’s history,” he remarked.

The first two chapters were inventing the technology and moving from grams to tons of production, he added. This phase is about reaching the mass market. Sila aims to begin manufacturing at the expanded facility in 2028, with output increasing over time.

Industry observers note that “None of this is easy,” Berdichevsky mentioned. “It’s not the inventing technology; it’s the manufacturing of it that’s really really hard, and we’re going to try to more than 10x the scale from what we’ve already done.”.

‘Absurd ambition’: Pulumi expands into software delivery with AI agents that ship and fix code

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.
  • Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle tech giant talked about building for years but always found too big to take on.
  • The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 8:57 amNovember 18, 2026 at 9:01 am.

Cloud-infrastructure startup Pulumi has a name for its current fiscal year, which started in July: “the year of absurd ambition.” The first results arrived Wednesday: two products the Seattle tech giant talked about building for years but always found too big to take on.

The products, Pulumi Delivery and Pulumi Agents, let AI agents take over more of the work of getting new software up and running, and fixing it when something breaks.

According to recent reports, “The ceiling on what we can accomplish is no longer limited by the speed at which we can build software,” mentioned Joe Duffy, the firm’s co-founder and CEO, recounting the message he delivered to the Pulumi team. “It’s limited by how ambitious we’re willing to be and how massive we’re willing to dream.”.

According to recent reports, the ambition is all the more notable because Pulumi is getting smaller. The firm has about 100 employees, down from about 130 last year. Duffy remarked there were no layoffs, and that AI has changed people’s roles and made the company more efficient.

Annual recurring revenue per employee more than doubled over the past year, he said. The firm isn’t profitable yet, but it has had a few months of positive cash flow this year. Pulumi hasn’t raised money since 2023, when it landed a $41 million round led by Madrona, bringing its total to about $99 million over the company’s lifetime.

Sources indicate that pulumi’s co-founders include Duffy and Eric Rudder, both Microsoft veterans. They started the company in 2017 to let engineers manage cloud infrastructure such as servers, networks and permissions by writing code in everyday languages like Python and TypeScript.

The new products take that approach further:.

Recent findings suggest that to decide whether a change is safe to ship, Pulumi Delivery can use Jev, an AI model from TypeSafe AI that estimates the odds of specific risks the team asks about in a planned change. If a risk is higher than the threshold the team sets, the release stops.

Sources indicate that duffy mentioned he first noticed TypeSafe in May when it signed up as a Pulumi customer, because he liked the name. A few months later, Jev took off and TypeSafe used Pulumi to expand worldwide.

“Now even the call on whether a change ships can be made by a model,” stated Daniel Gafni, a member of the technical staff at TypeSafe AI, in the Pulumi announcement. “That’s exactly the kind of decision we built Jev to make.”.

Both products are available now in public preview. Some features, including Jev decision gates and setting up agents, require Pulumi’s paid Pro or Enterprise intends.

Lucky timing: Pulumi’s founding bet on everyday programming languages turned out to suit AI agents, which are trained to be very good at writing exactly that kind of code.

“I wish I could say I predicted that 10 years ago, but it turns out in this case, what’s good for humans is also good for agents,” Duffy said.

In a recent development, AI agents now handle 40% of the operations on the Pulumi platform that people used to do, up from 15% in April and none in January, Duffy said. Agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pulumi’s own Neo are making infrastructure changes on their own.

According to recent reports, duffy said many companies building AI coding tools stop once the code is written and reviewed. “For them, life stops at the merge,” he said. The new products cover the steps after that, from testing through release.

Sources indicate that plenty of firm: Pulumi won’t have this market to itself. Duffy pointed to Harness, which calls it the “agentic SDLC” (short for software development lifecycle), and GitHub, which pitched “agentic software delivery” at its Universe conference last month. He stated Cursor aspires to solve the problem and Anthropic built its own internal system.

The upcoming products could replace some of the work now done by tools such as Argo CD and GitHub Actions, along with lots of homegrown scripts, he stated.

“This is an industry-changing moment, and somebody has to solve this problem,” Duffy stated. “And I think we are exceptionally well poised to do so.”.

Bring your own bot: Neo, the infrastructure agent Pulumi introduced last year, is now just one example of a Pulumi agent. Customers can set up as many as they want, each with its own job, instructions and tools. They can also bring their own agent, such as Claude Code or Codex, and run it in Pulumi’s cloud.

Neo itself, which ran mainly on Anthropic’s Claude, can now use models from OpenAI or Google, too. “It’s not just Anthropic anymore,” Duffy said.

Agents can start work from an alert in PagerDuty, Datadog or Honeycomb, on a schedule or on request, and they report back to teams in Slack.

In a recent development, pulumi has briefed about 50 customers, and about a dozen are in a private beta. Duffy said no launch in the manufacturer’s history has gotten a warmer reception, and he named Moderna among the customers eager to get it.

Pulumi has thousands of customers overall, including major companies such as BMW, Snowflake and Wiz.

The business: Pulumi’s gross margins have stayed in the high 80s to low 90s even as agents drive up usage, Duffy noted. Many customers run Pulumi from inside their own Claude Code sessions, which means they’re paying both Anthropic and Pulumi.

Recent findings suggest that duffy said Pulumi wasn’t out looking for money when it raised its last two rounds. Investors came to the company, and each deal came together in about 48 hours.

Madrona’s Tim Porter has joined the board, Duffy remarked, taking the seat previously held by the late Soma Somasegar, who led Pulumi’s first investment.

Recent findings suggest that about 40 of the manufacturer’s 100 employees are in the Seattle area, working out of an office at Two Union Square. Duffy said Pulumi is hiring more people locally because in-person work still matters when building new products.

Recent findings suggest that despite the smaller headcount, Pulumi is still hiring, including sales reps in nearly every region of the world. Inside the firm, Duffy mentioned Pulumi is having a lot of success with “product-minded engineers who can think from our customers’ point of view, who can think like engineering managers, commanding a team of agents.”.

It has been revealed that asked whether a sale or more funding was in the cards, Duffy said Pulumi aspires to be a long-term successful business. “There are a variety of ways to get there,” he said. “But we want to get there on our own terms.”.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.
  • This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.
  • With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue shows that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.

This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.

With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue shows that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.

Previous ETF data indicates that March remains the only month in which spot XRP ETFs have recorded net outflows since their launch.

While it still stands as the record outflow month for XRP ETFs, investors withdrew about $31.16 million from the funds during that month.

This means that the persistent withdrawals seen this month have brought the November outflow dangerously close to its previous monthly record seen in March.

Apparently, the spot XRP ETFs are on track to close November as their worst-performing month since launch, with just about $1 million left to hit the record.

Further data also reveals that the spot XRP ETFs have yet to record a single day of net inflows throughout November, as the persistent price decline has caused investors to slow down their purchases.

As such, the influx of fresh capital into the spot XRP ETF market has remained on hold amid growing market uncertainty and a shift in investor sentiment.

According to recent reports, dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, reacted to the recent market decline, which saw over $2.56 billion in liquidations. He hinted at weak demand as a possible reason behind the massive sell-off.

Markus earlier wrote in a post that "Black Friday came early." This came as the broader financial markets dropped, not just crypto: tech stocks, gold, copper, and Asian equities all fell.

Sources indicate that markus’s post garnered attention from the Dogecoin community and the wider crypto community. A Dogecoin community member responded: “Am I retarded for thinking crypto is about to go up?”.

@alphadoge777 well it always goes up and down 🤣 but the market has been looking pretty low demand for awhile now.

"Well, it always goes up and down," Markus said, pointing to crypto's inherent volatility and adding that the market had been experiencing "pretty low demand for a while now.".

His comments come as the crypto market continues to crash, highlighting concerns about the lack of buying interest needed to prop up prices.

Markus did not point to a specific catalyst for the decline, but his remarks highlight an crucial ingredient for a bullish comeback in the market: demand.

According to recent reports, the crypto market selloff deepened on Saturday, with Bitcoin hitting its lowest level since September 2024 and extending a brutal run for risk assets. Dogecoin was trading in the red, down 8.13% in the last 24 hours to $0.528 and down 16% weekly. Dogecoin fell to $0.05 earlier on Saturday, a low not seen since June 2022.

Data from Coinglass at press time show that $2.56 billion was liquidated in crypto positions over the past 24 hours; longs accounted for 89.2% of this total, at $2.28 billion, while short liquidations came in at $276,040.

Analysts pointed to rising real, or inflation-adjusted, U.S. Treasury yields as a key driver of the ongoing sell-off, which extends a bear market that began in October of last year.

Crypto investors are searching for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026. The broader crypto market has dropped since the Clarity Act faced a setback in September.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.
  • Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:48 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.

However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.

Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.

It has been revealed that the company’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company said. That segment was up 291% annually.

“We are now a different company, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.

The Street liked what it saw, with Dell’s stock rising more than 3% after hours, putting the brakes on an 11% decline earlier, during the regular trading session.

Dell’s performance in the quarter sets a fresh precedent for infrastructure systems companies, said longtime technology industry analyst Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research, SiliconANGLE Media’s sister market research firm.

In a recent development, “Dell has transformed from a PC company into a dominant enterprise infrastructure provider and industry bellwether,” he mentioned. “What’s most astounding to me is that I’ve always considered AWS to be Dell’s most formidable competitor. Dell is now significantly larger than AWS on a trailing 12-month revenue basis and is growing at a rate that’s more than double that of AWS, Azure and on a par with Google Cloud.”.

Dell is raising its forecast for AI servers in the coming fiscal years, and now sees sales rising to a staggering $78 billion, ahead of the Street’s target of $74 billion. At present, the manufacturer has an even bigger order backlog of $132.3 billion for AI servers. “Every order is verified for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” Clarke told analysts in response to a question about the reliability of that backlog.

Vellante stated Dell’s operating leverage is just as impressive, with its operating income, net profit and earnings per share all growing at rates over two-times its revenue growth.

“Its massive backlog and strong product execution allow it to be selective,” the analyst stated. “Thus the quality of its revenue and its backlog is very high, and the tech giant is well-positioned for the next several quarters. Current market signals point to a structural change in tech where vendors that are in a position to help customers transform and drive upcoming levels of productivity are poised to win over the long term. We increasingly see Dell as one of those leaders.”.

Besides servers, Dell still has a big business in the PC market. Its Client Services Group was once the tech giant’s biggest segment, but its revenue is now dwarfed by AI server sales. During the quarter, it generated revenue of $12.89 billion, below the Street’s forecast of $14.33 billion.

The reason for that miss is that the global PC market is presently enduring a sharp decline. Last month, Gartner Inc. reported a stunning 22% drop in global PC shipments in the third quarter, citing the increased costs of components such as memory chips, which have led to higher prices and compelled many people to hold onto their older laptops for longer.

According to recent reports, the miserable state of PC sales makes HP’s latest quarterly results seem even more impressive than they were. However, the company’s cautious outlook suggests that its incoming Chief Executive Emma Walmsley (pictured, right) will have her work cut out when she assumes the role full time on Jan. 4, when she’s slated to take over from interim CEO Bruce Broussard.

HP reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, surpassing the analyst consensus estimate that called for a profit of just 75 cents per share. Revenue for the period came to $16 billion, up 9% and above the Street’s target of $15.4 billion.

It has been revealed that HP’s stock briefly surged more than 17% after-hours, before promptly surrendering all of those gains in under an hour. It was down just under a percentage point at the time of writing.

Investors had low expectations of HP given the shoddy state of the PC market. The company has been trying to mitigate the situation somewhat by raising its prices, but it couldn’t stop its profit margins from declining in the quarter.

Recent findings suggest that the market was eagerly anticipating HP’s guidance to try and get a lid on whether or not the PC market has any prospect of recovery in the near future, but the tech giant disappointed by refusing to provide any. All it would say is that it forecasts free cash flow in the current quarter to be $3 billion, plus or minus $100 million. Analysts are targeting free cash flow of $3.3 billion.

In a recent development, HP hasn’t been helped by the fact that it has been without a CEO since PayPal Holdings Inc. surprisingly swooped in to poach its former leader Enrique Lores in February. Broussard has held the fort for close to nine months now, but the firm did at least finally name a successor in Walmsley, who will begin her tenure next year. She formerly led the pharmaceutical giant GSK Plc.

Walmsley has a tough act to follow, however, for Broussard has done rather well in his efforts to cope with the PC market downturn and the higher component costs. Although the stock was up and down today, it’s still up 25% in the year to date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charles Hoskinson’s Cardano is facing fresh criticism for struggling to attract users and generate on-chain activity, despite being nearly nine years into its development.

Widely-followed crypto analyst Lark Davis has branded the network a “largely failed blockchain,” pointing to a stark adoption gap with Solana, which launched four years later but has significantly outpaced ADA in daily users, perpetual futures trading volume, and application revenue.

It has been revealed that despite having nearly a decade to establish itself in the blockchain industry, Cardano continues to face questions about its ability to attract people and generate meaningful network activity. Analyst Lark Davis has commented on the adoption gap between Cardano and Solana, arguing that Solana has significantly outperformed ADA despite launching four years later.

“Nine years in and Cardano is still waiting on adoption,” Davis wrote on X.

Industry observers note that according to Davis, Cardano accounts for just around 1% of Solana’s daily users, highlighting the stark difference in activity between the two networks. The gap reportedly extends beyond user numbers, with Cardano recording only about 0.3% of Solana’s perpetual futures trading volume.

The revenue figures paint an even more challenging picture for the Cardano ecosystem. Davis estimates that Cardano generates roughly 0.2% of the application revenue recorded across Solana’s ecosystem, further highlighting the difference in economic activity between the competing networks.

Based on these figures, Davis delivered a particularly harsh assessment of Cardano, describing it as a “largely failed blockchain.” His criticism centers on the contrast between Cardano’s nine-year journey and Solana’s ability to build a considerably larger user base and generate more trading activity and application revenue in a shorter period.

The latest criticism follows a series of similar remarks from Davis about Cardano’s adoption challenges. As ZyCrypto previously reported, the analyst had also taken aim at Cardano over its relatively small user base, questioning the network’s ability to attract and retain people despite years of development.

Despite his harsh assessment of Cardano’s fundamentals, Davis has occasionally expressed optimism about ADA’s price prospects.

In November 2025, for instance, he suggested that Cardano could stage a rally similar to XRP’s 2024 surge, pointing to the strength of its community and brand as potential catalysts.

More recently, on September 28, Davis argued that Cardano’s “cult following” could help drive ADA back toward $1, with further upside potentially taking the token to $1.50 or even $2.

However, these bullish price projections focused more on speculative market demand and Cardano’s dedicated community than on measurable improvements in network adoption or ecosystem activity.

Benzinga News, Company Logos and Market Data Now Available Through Alpheya's AI-Powered Wealth Platform for Financial Institutions.

DETROIT, Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Benzinga, a leading provider of real-time financial news and market intelligence, today revealed an expanded data relationship with Alpheya, a wealth technology company headquartered in Abu Dhabi. Through this relationship, Alpheya will make Benzinga's real-time news and broader suite of data products available to banks and wealth management institutions.

According to recent reports, alpheya works with banks, family offices, and asset and wealth managers. Its platform gives these institutions a single cloud-based, AI-powered system for client apps, portfolio management and trading.

Many banks and private banks are now modernizing the digital experience they offer clients. To meet that shift, institutions want Benzinga market content inside their own mobile apps, so clients can follow their holdings without leaving the bank's platform. The agreement gives Alpheya's clients a direct path to that content.

Benzinga's news coverage includes earnings, analyst ratings, corporate events and breaking market headlines, giving investors context on the stocks they hold and trade. Beyond news, Benzinga's broader suite of structured market data products can support watchlists, portfolio views, research tools and trading workflows across Alpheya's platform.

"Banks are building wealth apps that compete with the best digital investing experiences anywhere, and the content inside those apps matters," said Clint Rhea, Manager of Institutional and Channel Partnerships at Benzinga. "Working with Alpheya gives banks and wealth managers a simple way to add Benzinga content through a platform they already rely on.".

"Wealth clients don't just need market news and data. They need to know what it means for their portfolio. With Benzinga inside the Alpheya platform, financial institutions can deliver trusted market intelligence, interpreted by Alpheya AI, so clients can act with confidence," stated Deepak Khanna, Chief Product Officer at Alpheya.

The agreement also builds on growing interest in Benzinga's data across the Middle East, adding a upcoming channel to the brokerages, trading platforms and fintech companies that already use Benzinga globally.

Recent findings suggest that about BenzingaBenzinga is a leading financial media and data technology company that empowers investors with high-quality, real-time market intelligence. Through its news platform, APIs, and data products, Benzinga provides traders, financial institutions, and fintech platforms with the insights they need to make smarter investment decisions. From breaking news and analyst ratings to corporate events and alternative datasets, Benzinga's tools help market participants stay ahead of the information that drives price movement.

To learn more, visit https://www.benzinga.com/apis/.

About AlpheyaAlpheya is a cloud-native, AI-powered wealth management platform headquartered in Abu Dhabi and built for financial institutions worldwide. Its modular B2B and B2B2C solutions support financial institutions' investors, relationship managers, advisors and portfolio managers, covering the full wealth journey from client onboarding and financial planning to portfolio management, trading, robo-advisory and performance reporting. At the heart of the platform are Alpheya's award-winning AI capabilities, including fully conversational AI journeys. Alpheya connects directly to an institution's back-end systems and to a wide ecosystem of brokers, market data and news providers.

Silicon Valley divorce lawyers see surge of CEO requests for prenups and partner NDAs after the Nvidia scandal

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Silicon Valley divorce lawyers are seeing surge in outreach from CEOs, founders, and high-net-worth employees who are citing the Nvidia scandal as the reason for their calls.
  • The revelation of Jensen Huang’s affairs, and Nvidia’s board subsequently firing him from the tech giant he founded, is a “precautionary tale for other CEOs,” said one lawyer who has been involved in the high-profile divorces of some of the tech industry’s most famous CEOs.
  • It has been revealed that although Huang’s board reinstated him on Monday in a controversial move, the roller coaster of events has pushed other CEOs to think about how their assets are connected, and potentially at risk, as a result of their personal relationships.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silicon Valley divorce lawyers are seeing surge in outreach from CEOs, founders, and high-net-worth employees who are citing the Nvidia scandal as the reason for their calls.

The revelation of Jensen Huang’s affairs, and Nvidia’s board subsequently firing him from the tech giant he founded, is a “precautionary tale for other CEOs,” said one lawyer who has been involved in the high-profile divorces of some of the tech industry’s most famous CEOs.

It has been revealed that although Huang’s board reinstated him on Monday in a controversial move, the roller coaster of events has pushed other CEOs to think about how their assets are connected, and potentially at risk, as a result of their personal relationships. In addition to pursuing prenuptial agreements, many are interested in drafting nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) for their significant others, which is a new trend, notes Monica Mazzei, a partner in Buchalter’s San Francisco family law office.

Sources indicate that “It’s totally changed the landscape,” said Mazzei. “I’ve never seen this before. This was definitely substantial news in the family law space.”.

It has been revealed that since the Nvidia scandal broke, three clients have contacted Mazzei with requests to draft NDAs for the significant others of CEOs. They specifically cited Huang in the outreach, mentioned Mazzei, who specializes in representing high-net-worth clients. Most of the requests are coming from the organization, not the CEO themselves, in an effort to protect the business.

“The organization is probably telling the CEO, ‘Anyone you need to date needs to sign this because we don’t want you to end up in a Jensen Huang situation,’” Mazzei said.

Huang had at least three known affairs, two with internal Nvidia employees, and one extra controversial relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at the Singapore-based organization Megaspeed. Alice Huang is reportedly suspected by some intelligence officials of being a Chinese spy and of illegally providing Chinese companies access to advanced Nvidia chips. The allegations are that Alice Huang is a “honeypot” who lured Jensen Huang into a relationship to get access to proprietary information.

Sources indicate that “Why honeypots work is because when you’re dating someone you’re not thinking about what they might overhear on a phone call, or see on papers lying out at home,” mentioned Mazzei. “They’re just in your life, overhearing a lot.”.

Recent findings suggest that demand for prenuptial agreements has also surged. Jensen and Lori Huang have been married for 41 years, and reportedly do not have a prenuptial agreement. Jensen Huang is one of the richest people in the world, with a net worth of roughly $137 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. According to California law, Lori stands to come away with half of that in a potential divorce, along with shares in Nvidia.

It remains to be seen if Lori Huang will file for a divorce. If the couple were to decide to split up, Lori and Jensen Huang would most likely agree to a settlement prior to the divorce proceedings becoming public, indicates Mazzei. Once the terms are finalized, Mazzei reckons, the couple would then go public with the news, as Jeff Bezos and Mackenzie Scott did.

Recent findings suggest that libby Leffler, founder and CEO of thisfirst.com, an online prenup service, says she’s seen more customers naming tech billionaires and founders as the inspiration for their agreements since the Nvidia scandal broke. Most of Leffler’s clients are founders and early employees at pre-IPO companies, especially in California and New York. Every time a public figure’s divorce or prenup makes headlines, Leffler’s inbound requests jump, but the naming of tech CEOs this time is different.

Recent findings suggest that “People used to name-check celebs, but now they are name-checking tech CEOs,” Leffler tells Fortune. “What they really mean is that they want to feel as protected as they assume those people are.” The most referenced arrangement is Jeff Bezos’s rumored prenuptial agreement with Lauren Sánchez, who became his second wife in 2025.

“Your relationship and your cap table are more connected than people think, and founders are seeing that play out,” Leffler noted.

Mazzei also noted a surge in prenup requests, specifically coming from Anthropic employees. When the company went public at a $1.5 trillion valuation on Nov. 19—a week after Huang’s ousting—it minted thousands of multimillionaires among the company’s relatively small staff of 5,300. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 18, 2026 at 10:01 amNovember 18, 2026 at 10:08 am.

Blue Origin’s engines look like they’re off the hook, at least for now.

The two BE-4 engines Blue Origin makes for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket weren’t to blame for the low thrust in Sunday’s failed launch, according to preliminary findings released Wednesday. Instead, it appears the engines didn’t get enough fuel from the rocket, ULA mentioned.

It has been revealed that in its latest update on the investigation, ULA noted it had completed an initial integrated review of flight data. Preliminary data indicate the first stage’s low thrust came from “inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines,” ULA said, adding that work remains to determine the cause.

According to recent reports, on Tuesday, ULA mentioned early data suggested the first stage underperformed just after liftoff, leaving the rocket too low and too slow to put 40 of Amazon’s Leo internet satellites into orbit. It didn’t say then whether the engines played a role.

According to recent reports, the BE-4s are made by Jeff Bezos’ Kent, Wash.-based Blue Origin. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp said Wednesday on X that he was proud of the BE-4 team for its “rapid response and support of ULA’s investigation” and that the organization looks forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.

In a recent development, the finding matters for Blue Origin beyond Vulcan. Its own Latest Glenn rocket uses seven BE-4s on its first stage, and Amazon has 24 New Glenn releases reserved for Leo.

Sources indicate that ULA repeated that Vulcan’s second stage appears to have started normally and that its RL10 engines operated as planned but couldn’t make up for the earlier loss of performance. The six Northrop Grumman solid rocket boosters, the source of problems on two earlier Vulcan flights, appear to have performed normally, ULA stated.

The Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing the ULA-led investigation. Amazon’s next Leo launch is an Ariane 6 mission carrying 36 satellites, targeted for no earlier than Nov. 23 from French Guiana.

ULA stated it will share more as the investigation continues.

Latest Update: Private equity deals in sports doubled in the past two years: Investors see it as an ‘institutional-grade asset class,’ Apollo’s Torsten Slok states

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Private equity is coming for America’s favorite pastime, America’s game, and almost every other sport.
  • According to recent reports, “Private equity deals in global sports have roughly doubled from about 100 a year in 2021–2023 to almost 200 in both 2024 and 2025, a sign that investors increasingly see sports as an institutional-grade asset class,” Slok wrote in a Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that the investment boom isn’t just limited to stakes in pro teams, however.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Private equity is coming for America’s favorite pastime, America’s game, and almost every other sport. Private equity firms are buying into sports at twice the pace they were a few years ago, according to Apollo Global Management chief economist Torsten Slok.

According to recent reports, “Private equity deals in global sports have roughly doubled from about 100 a year in 2021–2023 to almost 200 in both 2024 and 2025, a sign that investors increasingly see sports as an institutional-grade asset class,” Slok wrote in a Nov. 22 analysis.

Recent findings suggest that the investment boom isn’t just limited to stakes in pro teams, however. Private equity firms also target the businesses that supply, support and monetize sports, from equipment manufacturers to talent agencies to training facilities.

On Nov. 19, Swiss investment firm Partners Group agreed to acquire a majority stake in Rawlings Sporting Goods—the manufacturer of baseballs, gloves, bats, and protective equipment for MLB. The company serves as the league’s official supplier of game balls, gloves, helmets, face guards, and bases. The league itself owned a stake in the company as well, meaning unlike the minority stakes leagues allow in their teams, the deal gives a private equity firm control.

According to Partners Group, MLB and Rawlings’ existing shareholders will retain meaningful ownership while also giving the Swiss firm exposure to Rawlings’ broader business—which includes brands like Easton and Combat, as well as D-BAT Academies, a network of 228 indoor baseball and softball training facilities.

Sources indicate that “Rawlings’ iconic brands and training footprint helps reinforce participation in America’s pastime and has credibility with consumers and athletes across all ages,” Partners Group managing director, private equity goods and products, Thomas Clark mentioned in a press release. “We look forward to working with [CEO Ron Ostrowski], the Rawlings team, and MLB as long-term partners.”.

Apollo has its own sports arm as well: In August, Apollo Sports Capital became a “strategic investment partner” to MLB’s most iconic franchise—the New York Yankees. The deal was a $2.6 billion financing agreement with Yankee Global Enterprises, the team’s holding company, supporting the “continued growth” of the Yankees franchise while also refinancing its existing debt.

“Teams and leagues might embrace capital for any number of reasons: to support operating costs, update aging facilities or develop new venues, invest in new technologies, or grow their global reach,” Deloitte’s 2026 Global Sports Industry Outlook report read. “But outside investment brings greater scrutiny, new challenges, and rising expectations around transparency, governance, and financial rigor.”.

It has been revealed that for decades, professional sports restricted private equity firms and other institutional investors from owning stakes in their teams. Instead, franchises were controlled by wealthy individuals, families, or ownership groups—mainly from the leagues’ concern about preserving control over teams and maintaining structure.

Industry observers note that that began changing in 2019, however, when Major League Baseball became the first major U.S. professional sports league to permit private equity investments in franchises. The NBA and Major League Soccer followed in 2020, and the NHL lifted restrictions in 2021. The NFL became the last of the four major American sports leagues to approve private equity ownership, in 2024.

Recent findings suggest that but those permissions came with limits. According to Sportico, MLB allowed institutional investors to own up to 30% of a franchise, with a single fund capped at 15%. The NBA and NHL permit up to 30% institutional ownership per team as well, but cap individual funds at 20%. The NFL has the strictest ownership rules, only allowing approved private equity firms to own a combined stake of up to 10% in a team—and only 10% in an individual fund as well.

It has been revealed that and the owners have taken advantage of that influx of capital. Outside money helps owners pay for stadium construction, arena renovations, player contracts, and the development of surrounding entertainment districts, all without having to foot the full bill themselves.

For example, the Buffalo Bills created an arrangement in 2024 following the NFL’s lifted restrictions to sell 21% of the team’s stake to a group of limited partners—which included a 10% investment from private equity firm Arctos Partners. The transaction came as the Bills were building their new stadium, when projected costs rose from $1.4 billion to $2.1 billion.

Sources indicate that but the benefit for private equity owners exists as well. Professional sports teams have access to multiple revenue streams, including broadcasting rights, ticket sales, sponsorships, merchandise, licensing, and stadium-related businesses. The five major U.S. professional sports leagues generated approximately $60 billion in combined revenue in 2025, according to Congress. The estimated combined value of their franchises reached approximately $560 billion that year.

“The upcoming model of baseball—or basketball, football—is teams becoming media companies and transcending a local marketplace,” Rashaun Williams, founder and chief investment officer of Harbinger Sports Partners, which held a minority stake in the newly relocated Las Vegas Athletics MLB team, previously told Fortune. “They’re finding ways to diversify their revenue and monetize that fan base 365 days a year.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc.
  • Industry observers note that bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well.
  • Industry observers note that marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 18:49 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc. has closed a huge $227 million seed round led by Accel.

Industry observers note that bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well. They were joined by a large group of angel investors that included the chief executives of Palo Alto Networks Inc, Uber Technologies Inc., Box Inc. and Dropbox Inc. GeekWire reported on Monday that Marlowe is valued at $1.15 billion.

Industry observers note that marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan. Lewis previously headed the Microsoft Corp. unit responsible for Copilot Studio, the tech giant’s AI agent development tool. Srinivasan was the techical lead of the firm’s AI infrastructure group.

Marlowe is building AI data centers for inference workloads. The company will optimize each facility for a specific inference workload category by tailoring its chip mix, network configuration and software. Marlowe believes that its approach will provide better hardware efficiency than general-purpose graphics card clusters.

“Even modest gains in network architecture, power oversubscription, AI-driven fleet operations, and workload-specific inference optimization multiply to create a durable, 2-3x overall advantage in performance, availability, resiliency, and cost,” Lewis and Srinivasan wrote in Marlowe’s launch blog post.

The organization looks to bring its first data center online  next month. It’s based on hardware from Etched Inc., an inference chip startup that was valued at $21 billion in August.

Graphics cards often use only a small fraction of their maximum clock speed to avoid overheating. Etched’s chip is less prone to overheating and can therefore operate at higher clock speeds, which boosts model performance. The firm notes that its accelerator provides “multiple times the FLOPs density” of graphics cards.

Etched ships its chips as part of custom-made inference racks. According to the company, the systems feature an interconnect that can perform some data movement tasks more than four times faster than competing silicon. Etched’s rack design also includes custom power management and cooling components.

Marlowe’s second facility will come online in the second quarter of 2027. It will host racks based on Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s Helios design. A Helios rack hosts 72 AMD graphics cards along with central processing units and Pensando data processing units, or DPUs. The DPUs offload networking tasks from the other chips to leave more computing capacity for AI models.

Sources indicate that helios racks’ networking and power delivery links are arranged in a configuration that reduces the need for manual cable maintenance. Additionally, the coolant lines feature a so-called quick-disconnect design. They can be plugged and unplugged without the specialized tools usually needed for the task.

It has been revealed that geekWire reported that Marlowe has also signed a letter of intent for a third data center. According to the publication, each of the company’s planned facilities will provide tens of megawatts of computing capacity. One megawatt is enough to power several hundred homes.

Marlowe will use the proceeds from its seed round to finance hardware purchases and hire engineers.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, Binance is witnessing a rapid surge in its futures trading activity as the broader crypto market continues to face increased selling pressure.

While the market is still struggling with volatility and rapidly declining investor interest, the latest on-chain data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that futures traders have become extremely active on Binance.

The data highlights that both Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen their perpetual futures trading volume on Binance surge to a combined high of $39.8 billion as of November 20.

Notably, this marks the highest level the metric has reached since September 21, indicating that traders are actively adjusting their positions to hedge against further losses as volatility continues to intensify.

Nonetheless, Bitcoin saw the highest increase in perpetual futures volume as it surged to $24.75 billion on the same day.

The data further indicated that the volume was slightly higher than the $24.57 billion recorded on September 21, when Bitcoin was trading above $87,000.

Ethereum, on the other hand, followed with a notable increase in the same metric, recording $15.05 billion in perpetual futures volume on the same day.

However, Ethereum did not entirely mimic Bitcoin in the trend as this was still below the $17.27 billion recorded during the September 21 trading period.

Further data shows that the high futures trading activity recorded on Binance on November 20 has coincided with BlackRock’s record Bitcoin ETF outflow.

The data indicates that BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $511 million in net outflows on that day, marking a sharp reversal from the positive inflows seen in September.

While this highlights that investors are also pulling their funds from Bitcoin ETFs, it marked the highest single-day outflow BlackRock has ever recorded.

Blockchain developers have long struggled to process high transaction volumes without slowing down network agreement. As digital payment systems expand, developers are exploring parallel processing to increase capacity across separate locations. Because traditional blockchains process transactions sequentially, high demand often triggers severe congestion and rising user fees during peak market activity.

#190642. Tech Report: On a $1,000 Social Security check, Medicare’s 2027 premium hike eats 18% of the COLA raise—and hits small checks the hardest

Tech Report: On a $1,000 Social Security check, Medicare’s 2027 premium hike eats 18% of the COLA raise—and hits small checks the hardest

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fortune

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in 2027, Social Security recipients will get their biggest cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in four years.
  • According to recent reports, most COLA announcements fail to emphasize that Medicare takes its slice first.
  • Although $6.50 doesn’t sound like much, it absorbs about 9% of the average retiree’s raise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in 2027, Social Security recipients will get their biggest cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) in four years. January’s benefits will be 3.6% higher, lifting the average retired worker’s monthly check to about $2,170, according to the Social Security Administration’s 2027 COLA announcement. The larger adjustment reflects persistent inflation in 2026.

According to recent reports, most COLA announcements fail to emphasize that Medicare takes its slice first. Starting in January, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services declared on Nov. 17 that the standard Part B premium rises by $6.50 to $209.40 a month. For most retirees, that premium is deducted straight from their Social Security benefit.

Although $6.50 doesn’t sound like much, it absorbs about 9% of the average retiree’s raise. And because the premium is a flat amount, the smaller the check, the bigger the share it takes.

Recent findings suggest that for a retiree collecting the 2026 average of $2,095 a month, the 3.6% COLA adds about $75. After the higher premium, roughly $69 remains, so Medicare claims about 9% of the increase.

It has been revealed that lower down the scale, the bite grows. A $1,000 monthly benefit rises by $36, but only $29.50 survives the premium hike, an 18% haircut on the raise. At $1,500 a month, the COLA is worth $54 and the net gain is $47.50, meaning 12% of the raise goes to Medicare.

Recent findings suggest that bigger checks barely feel it. A $2,500 benefit gains $90 and keeps $83.50, losing 7% of the increase. At $3,000 a month, the raise is $108, the net gain is $101.50, and the premium takes just 6%.

That math applies to retirees who pay the standard premium out of their benefits. Higher-income enrollees pay income-based surcharges on top of it, while states cover the Part B premium for about one in five Medicare enrollees with low incomes and savings.

By recent standards, this year’s hike is mild. The 3.2% premium increase is smaller than the COLA for the first time since 2023; in 2026, the premium jumped 9.7% against a 2.8% COLA.

Even though COLAs are treated like bonuses or raises, they’re not. As David Herbert, director of economics & economic freedom and a senior research fellow at the American Institute for Economic Research (AIER), told The Hill, “It’s meant to make sure that Social Security recipients are receiving the same amount of spending power as they did in the past. It’s not actually going to make them wealthier or have an easier time buying things that they weren’t already going to buy.”.

In a recent development, seniors appear to agree. In an AARP survey conducted before the announcement, 80% of Social Security recipients noted a projected 3.5% COLA in 2027 would not keep up with rising prices. When the final number landed, some retirees dismissed it as too little to offset soaring costs.

Recent findings suggest that it seems as though seniors are right. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported 3.7% annual inflation for September 2026, its most recent annual figure. The 3.6% COLA will not keep up, especially since the higher payments don’t start until January.

By then, seniors will have absorbed higher prices since March, when inflation hit 3.3% and outpaced the 2026 COLA of 2.8%. It peaked at 4.2% in May. In other words, a 3.6% COLA is a small improvement, but it comes too late.

Against the backdrop of higher benefits and costs looms Social Security’s insolvency. The 2026 Trustees Report found that starting in the fourth quarter of 2032, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) Trust Fund will no longer be able to pay 100% of scheduled benefits. Instead, recipients would receive only 78% of them.

Part of the funding shortfall comes down to demographics. According to the trustees’ projections, about 2.6 workers paid in for every beneficiary in 2025, compared with 41.9 in 1945. The trustees expect the ratio to keep falling, to about 1.9 workers per beneficiary by 2075.

With fewer workers paying into Social Security, “Congress is going to have to step in and do something,” remarked Herbert. “What is going to be left over for people who are not quite at retirement but are hoping at some point to see any form of a return on investment on this money that we’ve been sending the federal government for our entire working lives?”.

That job falls to the newly introduced Congress, which convenes in January and has roughly six years to act before automatic cuts kick in. In the meantime, Herbert advises those a decade or two from retirement to start saving and investing. More importantly, workers shouldn’t strategy on receiving full Social Security benefits in retirement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.

Consumers reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.

Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some users claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.

The cause the glitch is still unclear, while the reported transactions are yet to be verified.

The incident might have involved thin liquidity problem in Kraken's CAD order books.

Large sell orders reportedly overwhelmed available buy orders, leaving insufficient demand to absorb the selling pressure.

According to some accounts, at one point about 20 BTC was being sold every 15 minutes, causing the imbalance to push BTC price against CAD further down.

According to recent reports, one such transaction resulted in BTC price at around C$24,250, or $16,900. Compared with Bitcoin trading between $57,000-$58,000, the discount amounted to a staggering 71%. Other customers reported BTC briefly trading around $27,000.

Kraken's status page continued to show its systems as operational during the incident. No official explanation from the exchange was available at the time of writing.

Recent findings suggest that the reported dislocation highlights the risks associated with trading in markets with limited liquidity. When an order book lacks sufficient buy-side depth, even relatively large sell orders can cause prices to move sharply away from the broader market.

On Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

It has been revealed that liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Sources indicate that bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETH/USDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

Tech Report: ‘Sister isn’t free’: Melinda French Gates fact-checks viral ‘SNL’ sketch on eldercare

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm.
  • A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.
  • The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm.

A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.

The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.

French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up:.

Recent findings suggest that sister will provide. True, French Gates remarked, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care.

It has been revealed that she’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason.

In a recent development, paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” Newly introduced America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000.

Sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers remarked they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did.

Recent findings suggest that “Free” is misleading. French Gates mentioned Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life.

French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024.

She left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S.

The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research.

It has been revealed that in its own analysis, The Fresh York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers.

French Gates said she welcomed the conversation.

“I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”.

webAI Releases TwIL-8B: A 5 GiB Open-Weight Reasoning Model With a 98.2 MATH-500 Score

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • webAI's open-weight TwIL-8B posts 98.2 on MATH-500 and claims it tops Gemma 4 31B.
  • It has been revealed that A model small enough to run from a roughly 5 GiB file on a CPU now claims a 98.2 on MATH-500.
  • webAI released TwIL-8B as an open-weight model on November 4, and its Hugging Face model card leads with ambitious numbers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

webAI's open-weight TwIL-8B posts 98.2 on MATH-500 and claims it tops Gemma 4 31B. The card's own footnotes show why the comparison deserves a re-run.

It has been revealed that A model small enough to run from a roughly 5 GiB file on a CPU now claims a 98.2 on MATH-500. The most revealing line in its model card isn't a score, though. It's a footnote saying the competitor numbers were never re-run.

webAI released TwIL-8B as an open-weight model on November 4, and its Hugging Face model card leads with ambitious numbers. The 8.8B-parameter reasoning model is post-trained from IBM's Granite 4.2 8B using full-parameter supervised fine-tuning, followed by GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning. A final length-aware RL stage produces the "balanced" variant, which is the default.

It has been revealed that the card reports 98.2 on MATH-500 and 88.3 on AIME 2025. It notes TwIL-8B posts the highest MATH-500 and LiveCodeBench scores in its comparison group, which includes Gemma 4 31B at about 3.5 times its size. That claim is worth testing, because small models that beat larger ones are exactly what open-weight users want to hear.

According to recent reports, on MATH-500, the card lists TwIL-8B at 98.2, Qwen3.5-9B at 96.6 and Gemma 4 31B at 87.9. On AIME 2025, TwIL-8B scores 88.3 against 87.1 for Gemma 4 31B. On LiveCodeBench, TwIL-8B scores 81.6 against 80.0, though that figure carries a dagger marking it as measured on the verbose variant, not the default balanced one.

The card is also more candid than most. It indicates TwIL-8B is not a knowledge model. GPQA Diamond comes in at 70.2, trailing Gemma 4 31B by 14.1 points, and the model also trails on MMLU-Pro and HLE. There is no safety or preference tuning beyond what Granite carries, and the license is non-commercial. That honesty makes the claims easier to weigh.

Here is where the headline gets complicated. TwIL-8B's scores come from webAI's own internal high-effort pass@1 runs. The card states that competitor scores are published figures and were not re-run.

In a recent development, gemma 4 31B's 87.9 on MATH-500 comes from Red Hat's evaluation of an FP8 build, using the lighteval harness, not from Google. The card itself notes that this figure is unusually low and may reflect answer extraction. In other words, the 10.3-point gap that anchors the headline compares one team's own harness against a third party's number that the card suspects may be understated.

None of this makes TwIL-8B's result wrong. It means the margin isn't established until both models run under the same harness, prompt and sampling settings. For reference, Google's Gemma 4 model card is the source for several of the other Gemma figures in the table.

In a recent development, read the whole table and the picture is more balanced than the headline suggests. In the card's head-to-head summary, TwIL-8B beats Gemma 4 31B on 3 of 14 shared benchmarks and loses 11. It leads on MATH-500, LiveCodeBench and AIME 2025, but trails on AIME 2026 (88.3 against 89.2), HMMT Feb 2026 (68.2 against 77.2), GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and IFEval.

The AIME 2025 lead is the shakiest. The card indicates AIME and HMMT sets have 30 to 33 problems, so one problem is worth about 3 points, and gaps of that size sit within noise. A 1.2-point margin is well under one problem, so the result is best read as a tie.

Against the closest same-size rival, Qwen3.5-9B, the card reveals the models roughly level on contest math, with TwIL-8B using fewer tokens: about 19.5k per AIME 2026 problem against 31.2k. That efficiency claim may turn out to be the more durable one.

Industry observers note that the card makes replication unusually practical. The Q4_K_M balanced GGUF weighs 4.98 GiB and runs through llama.cpp, with a command given in the card. Larger Q8_0 and F16 builds exist only for the verbose variant. The model also needs a big generation budget, since a short limit truncates its reasoning and scores far worse. The card suggests settings around 32,768 new tokens and a 40,960-token context.

Anyone planning a check should expect three catches. First, the card indicates all its scores were measured on bf16 weights, not the GGUF builds, so a CPU run tests a slightly different artifact, and the card expects small deviations, most likely at Q4_K_M. Second, MATH-500 is 500 problems and each answer can run to tens of thousands of tokens, so CPU testing will be slow. Third, the decoding setup matters, since the card says none of its numbers use low-effort or thinking-off modes.

For a fair comparison, the same prompt, answer extraction and sampling must be applied to Gemma 4 31B too, ideally at full precision.

Industry observers note that the card also lists contamination caveats. Its training pools were decontaminated against AIME, HMMT Feb 2025 and 2026, MATH-500, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, HLE, IFEval, IFBench and LiveCodeBench using 13-gram matching. HMMT Nov 2025 and the HumanEval, MBPP and CRUXEval suites weren't in the decontamination set. The MATH-500 and AIME results fall inside the protected group, which counts in the model's favor.

According to recent reports, overall, TwIL-8B looks like a genuinely strong small model for contest math, code and instruction following, and the card is open about its weak spots. The claim to beat Gemma 4 31B is narrower than the headline suggests: a clear lead on one benchmark, a likely tie on another and a loss on most of the rest.

The useful next step is a same-harness run of both models, with the bf16 weights as a control for the GGUF build. Until independent results appear, the 98.2 is best quoted as webAI's reported figure, and the size-beating framing is better described as unproven than wrong.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta employees have raised concerns about the organization’s Muse AI agent after receiving unprompted notifications that tapped into private information, according to internal posts seen by Reuters.
  • In one example, a Meta staffer reported that Muse sent her a reminder on her personal phone to respond to a message from her sister on the encrypted messaging service Signal.
  • Sources indicate that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have raised concerns about the organization’s Muse AI agent after receiving unprompted notifications that tapped into private information, according to internal posts seen by Reuters.

In one example, a Meta staffer reported that Muse sent her a reminder on her personal phone to respond to a message from her sister on the encrypted messaging service Signal.

Sources indicate that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee posted.

A Meta colleague also shared that he got unsolicited chats related to apps he had not connected and discovered Muse was set up by default with permission to access push notifications on Android phones, Reuters reported.

Another employee posted that during his chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, Muse mentioned, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

Other random Muse messages also took Meta workers aback, including a question about parental control over access to their child’s data and a conversation about picking up a coffee table that raised concern over “possible cross-account context leak.”.

In response to the internal posts about Muse, a member of Meta’s Superintelligence team mentioned the agent appeared to be hallucinating, owing to built-in prompts that were designed to engage customers between sessions, according to Reuters.

“These (hallucinations) unfortunately bias towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks,” he mentioned, adding that other cases involved “crypto-related things too, like giving people updates on their Bitcoin balances.”.

The random, out-of-context messages were confirmed as hallucinations.

A Meta spokesperson stated employee testing is core to product development and is meant to generate feedback in order to implement privacy safeguards, adding that employees have access to versions of Muse that are different from those the public has and that some functions aren’t available elsewhere.

As for the Muse messages that referred to encrypted Signal chats, the spokesperson pointed out that Android consumers have the option to grant apps notification access, which they must opt in to and is not specific to Muse.

“With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on,” Meta explained.

Recent findings suggest that since Muse was launched in September, it’s been downloaded more than 10 million times, becoming one of the fastest-growing apps ever. It’s also key to the social media giant’s proposal to generate billions of dollars in revenue from AI.

But other companies are blocking Muse and other AI agents. For example, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon noted the bank won’t allow agents to access customer accounts and act on their behalf.

Similarly, Amazon won’t let Muse shop on its e-commerce platform and is already fighting to keep out Perplexity’s AI agents.

The process of raising those barriers, however, also entails network upgrades that may be contributing to a sudden surge in outages.

In recent weeks, companies like Chase, Wells Fargo, United Airlines, Apple, and Microsoft saw temporary service disruptions. U.S. officials have remarked there’s no evidence of cyberattacks, suggesting software patches were deployed before all the bugs were worked out.

Industry observers note that because AI tools can find vulnerabilities faster than companies can safely fix them, the pressure to fix them right away is straining systems that were never designed for that speed, Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, told the Financial Times.

In an interview with Fortune’s Catherina Gioino, Mark Giles, director of Downdetector parent company Ookla Research, said there’s nothing linking the outages.

“This is a substantial blip, but it’s kind of on par for the course for what we’re seeing in terms of those longer-term trends,” he said. “Most of the time they’re fairly self-contained and remedied quite quickly. It’s the ones where you can’t withdraw money or you can’t access your emails that really get the headlines.”.
